study_identification.title: Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project

study_characteristics.study_objective: To characterize heterogeneity in autism by identifying patterns of neural diversity as reflected in BOLD fMRI in the way individuals with autism engage with a varied array of cognitive tasks.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Participants were required to have acceptable overlap (> 94%) with the MNI152 standard brain after image registration. We then excluded 57 participants due to poor overlap (< 50%) with one or more particular regions from the ICP brain parcellation atlas. Participants were furthermore excluded on the basis of incidental findings and incomplete scans (N = 18), and those in the top 5% in terms of head motion quantified through root mean square framewise displacement (N = 27).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat was used to clean the data for linear site effects.

predictor_effects.answer: A normative model of potency edge values was built against age and sex from typically developing participants.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper mentions handling site effects with ComBat and correcting for age and sex in the normative model. However, it does not provide a comprehensive discussion or evaluation of how other potential nuisance structures were handled.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: ComBat was used to clean the data for linear site effects. ... A normative model of potency edge values was built against age and sex from typically developing participants using the nispat implementation in python. This means that downstream analyses are also inherently corrected for age and sex.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not mention any validation of the normative model using non-independent data within the same domain.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper uses out-of-sample cross-validation to assess the stability and generalizability of the CCA parameters, which is a form of independent validation within the same domain.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Stability and generalizability of CCA parameters was assessed through 1000 different splits of tenfold out-of-sample cross-validation-building a 'test' distribution of the first canonical correlation as well as the paired CCA weights.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not mention any validation of the normative model using data from a different domain.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to relate connectome data to behavioral data.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individuals with autism engage with tasks in a globally atypical way, but the particular spatial pattern of this atypicality is nevertheless similar across tasks.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Deviation from the normative ranges of global functional connectivity was greater for individuals with autism compared to TD in each fMRI task paradigm (all tasks p < 0.001). The similarity across individuals of the deviation pattern was significantly increased in autistic relative to TD individuals (p < 0.002). The CCA identified significant and robust brain-behavior covariation between functional connectivity atypicality and autism-related behavioral features.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Test-retest variability in functional connectivity. The normative range estimation necessitates that the typically developing participants are treated as a single group, potentially masking subgroups in autism.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study used a novel task potency approach which combines the unique aspects of both resting state fMRI and task-fMRI to quantify task-induced variations in the functional connectome.
